components.name: Live Lamp
components.description: A lit point in a bezel: running in production.

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a room, not a page of project cards. Artur's shipped products run as glass app windows floating at staggered depths over the ridgelines of the Serra Fluminense, and the visitor walks that room by scrolling: the camera stops in front of each product while its chapter is read, cranes up into the night sky for the long reading chapters, and comes back down to the whole workspace at dawn for the close. Every window is a working simulation of the real product (an AI chat failing over between LLM providers, OCR reading a medicine box, a franchise dashboard settling royalties), always tagged as synthetic data.

Light carries the narrative and glass is the only material. The DOM floats over a fixed WebGL stage; copy sits on frosted panels on the left, the camera frames the subject on the right. One family, Mona Sans, carries every voice by moving along its width axis.
keyCharacteristics: A fixed 3D room behind every chapter; chapters declare a camera frame, scrolling flies between them.
Products shown working, not described: seven live app-window simulations.
Three lights only: ember dusk, deep night, dawn.
Frosted glass with a lit top rim as the single surface treatment.
Warm-white ink and pills; color lives in the sky and inside each product's own window.

rules.name: The Three Lights Rule
rules.body: The room has exactly three lights, dusk at the hero, night for the reading chapters, dawn at the contact, and scroll blends between them. A new chapter takes one of these phases; it never introduces a fourth light.

rules.name: The Own-Window Rule
rules.body: A product accent appears only inside that product's window and its chapter. No accent is used for interface chrome, links or section headings.

rules.name: The Live Rule
rules.body: Live Green means "running in production" and nothing else.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed through weight and the width axis together (wdth 104 → 110). Never add a second display family for emphasis.

rules.name: The Real-Number Rule
rules.body: Metrics use tabular numerals and render their real value server-side; the odometer only animates from zero to that value, and a screen reader always gets the final number.

rules.name: The Open-Half Rule
rules.body: On phones the top half of each product chapter stays empty (panels start at 50svh, the hero copy at 42svh) so the chapter's window is seen before its panel slides over it. The camera steps back until the subject fits the width and lifts it into that half.

rules.name: The One-Room Rule
rules.body: All seven windows live in one continuous space; a chapter changes where the camera stands, never swaps in a new scene.

rules.name: The Depth-of-Field Rule
rules.body: Only the windows the current chapter is about are sharp; everything else steps back. Wide shots (hero, reading chapters, contact) have no focus and nothing dims.

rules.name: The Rim-Light Rule
rules.body: Glass is lit from above by a single inset highlight; edges stay hairline. Never outline glass with a bright full border or an outer glow.

rules.name: The Concentric Rule
rules.body: An inner surface's radius is its container's radius minus the gap between them; nested corners never look parallel-offset.

dos: **Do** show each product working inside its own window, with synthetic data tagged as such, and keep every claim in the panels real.
**Do** give every new chapter a camera frame and one of the three lights.
**Do** keep copy on frosted panels over the room, left on desktop and in the lower half on phones.
**Do** honor reduced motion with camera cuts, finished windows and static counters.
**Do** keep the page complete without WebGL: the painted dusk and ridges carry it.
donts: **Don't** lay products out as a grid of cards or screenshots; the room is the layout.
**Don't** use a product accent outside its own window and chapter.
**Don't** add a fourth light or a light-mode variant of the room.
**Don't** outline glass with bright borders or outer glows.
**Don't** animate anything on load beyond the hero claim and its staggered lines.
**Don't** use bounce or elastic easing; the system eases out exponentially (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`).
